hero.title: File:Hawker Hunter F.2 ‘WN904’ (27854868258).jpg
hero.artist: Alan Wilson from Stilton, Peterborough, Cambs, UK
hero.description:
c/n S4/U/2912.
Built 1954.
British military serial WN904.
Among the 1,972 Hunters built, the F.2 was a rare mark. It was powered, along with the F.5, by the 8,300lbf Armstrong Siddeley Sapphire 101, instead of the Rolls-Royce Avon used in all other marks of Hunter. 
Built by Armstrong Whitworth at Coventry, only 45 were produced and this is now the only surviving example.
Delivered to 257sqn at Wattisham in September 1954, she remained with the unit until severely damaged in January 1956. Although repaired, she was then stored until 1958 when she went to the Melksham School of Technical Training as ‘7544M’.
In 1974 she was donated to the Imperial War Museum collection at Duxford, but was later loaned out to serve as a gate guard at Waterbeach Barracks, the former RAF Waterbeach. 
She is now painted in 56sqn markings and is on permanent display at the Sywell Aviation Museum.
Sywell Aerodrome, Northamptonshire, UK.

21st May 2017

gallery.title: File:Cockpit of North American Harvard IIb -KF650- (41728425911).jpg
gallery.artist: Alan Wilson from Stilton, Peterborough, Cambs, UK
gallery.description:
c/n 14-2441.
British military serial KF650.
Built in January 1944 and delivered directly to the RAF, this Harvard was written off when it overturned while landing at Syerston on 14th May 1954. 
Privately owned as part of the Midland Aircraft Recovery Group, the restored cockpit section is seen while loaned for display at the Sywell Aviation Museum.
Sywell Aerodrome, Northamptonshire, UK.

gallery.filename: De Havilland Canada DHC1 Chipmunk T.10 PAX ‘WG419’ (41728424461).jpg
gallery.title: File:De Havilland Canada DHC1 Chipmunk T.10 PAX ‘WG419’ (41728424461).jpg
gallery.artist: Alan Wilson from Stilton, Peterborough, Cambs, UK
gallery.description:
c/n C1/0493.
Built 1951 as a standard T.10 with the British military serial WG419. After June 1972 it was reduced to a fuselage section and used for ground instruction as ‘8206M’. Officially these were designated as Chipmunk T.10 (PAX), but were often known simply as ‘Chippax’.
It later came under the control of 1053sqn Air Training Corps (ATC) at Armthorpe, but is now on display at the Sywell Aviation Museum.
Sywell Aerodrome, Northamptonshire, UK.

gallery.filename: Rolls-Royce Merlin from Hawker Hurricane I -P3162- (40829403435).jpg
gallery.title: File:Rolls-Royce Merlin from Hawker Hurricane I -P3162- (40829403435).jpg
gallery.artist: Alan Wilson from Stilton, Peterborough, Cambs, UK
gallery.description:
From the adjacent information in the museum:-
“This is the engine from a Hawker Hurricane fighter aircraft, serial number P3162, flown by Flt Sgt I K J Bidgood which crashed on 2nd June 1941 at Terrington St john, Norfolk, after a mid-air collision with another Hurricane W9114. Both pilots took to their parachutes but neither survived. It would seem that they bailed out too low and their parachutes did not have time to open. Both pilots were Battle of Britain veterans.
P3162 had previously served and survived the Battle of Britain with 111, 253, 303 and 71 Squadrons before being delivered to 56 Operational Training Unit at RAF Sutton Bridge, from where it was operating when it crashed“
The recovered engine is on display at the Sywell Aviation Museum.
Sywell Aerodrome, Northamptonshire, UK.

21st May 2017

gallery.filename: Bristol Hercules XVI engines from Vickers Wellington B.X -LN482- (26860160917).jpg
gallery.title: File:Bristol Hercules XVI engines from Vickers Wellington B.X -LN482- (26860160917).jpg
gallery.artist: Alan Wilson from Stilton, Peterborough, Cambs, UK
gallery.description:
Built in 1943, LN482 was one of 3,406 Wellingtons produced by the Vickers factory at Chester (Hawarden).
Coded ‘OP-B’, it was being operated from RAF Westcott by No11  Operational Training Unit when it crashed at Rothersthorp Village, Northamptonshire on 5th April 1944, with the loss of all six crew.
The two engines and various other parts have been recovered and are now on display at the Sywell Aviation Museum.
Sywell Aerodrome, Northamptonshire, UK.

21st May 2017

gallery.filename: Nose of English Electric Canberra TT.18 -WH887- ‘847’ (27854870128).jpg
gallery.title: File:Nose of English Electric Canberra TT.18 -WH887- ‘847’ (27854870128).jpg
gallery.artist: Alan Wilson from Stilton, Peterborough, Cambs, UK
gallery.description:
c/n EEP2385 / SH.1644.
British military serial WH887.
Built in 1954 as a standard B.2 bomber variant for the RAF. Transferred to the Royal Navy in November 1969 and converted to a TT.18 for use as a target tug. Retired in November 1992 and ferried to RAE Llanbedr as a source of spares. Finally being dismantled and disposed of in 2004. 
The nose was preserved and is now on display at the Sywell Aviation Museum.
Sywell Aerodrome, Northamptonshire, UK.

21st May 2017
